subject.title: Feature: fire session-memory hook on session reset/prune, not just compaction

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable session-memory lifecycle contract for both lazy resets and session-store pruning, or should only the daily/idle reset slice proceed through #61675?
rationale: The requested behavior changes when and how transcripts are persisted, crosses internal hooks and plugin hooks, and overlaps an open reset-only PR while leaving prune semantics unresolved.

options.title: Canonical lifecycle design
options.body: Keep #51572 as the canonical design item and require one privacy-aware contract covering lazy reset and prune before implementation.

options.title: Land reset slice first
options.body: Use #61675 or a replacement to handle daily/idle resets now, then track prune as a separate follow-up with its own contract.

options.title: Decline prune hooks
options.body: Limit session-memory to reset/command boundaries and close the prune portion as out of scope for core hook semantics.

recommendation.title: Canonical lifecycle design
recommendation.body: Keep #51572 as the canonical design item and require one privacy-aware contract covering lazy reset and prune before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent reset-hook history and the active related PR make this the closest available routing owner for the maintainer choice.
